rendered: The premise does not hold: the document does not show bare Al outperforming carbon/Al at high current. Bare Al did worse at high current. The paper says that bare Al electrodes were prone to[1] failure at these currents, cited to the supplementary Figure S3[2]. The authors attribute bare Al's earlier shorting to we attribute to the uneven plating that occurs due to the higher[3] nucleation overpotential, and say the carbon/Al electrodes gave more stable plating and stripping with higher Coulombic efficiency. For carbon/Al, the paper reports a voltage hysteresis of 45 mV[4] at 4 mA/cm^2[5], which it calls low even at high currents. The document gives no bare Al hysteresis value at that current, so it cannot say how much lower the bare Al hysteresis was. The only hysteresis comparison at that current is with earlier Cu electrodes, which nearly double the hysteresis at[6] 4 mA/cm^2[7] (comparison shown in the supplementary Figure S4[8]). The averaging 14 mV[9] figure is a separate long-term result over more than 1000[10] cycles, from the panel described as cycles performed at 0.5 mA/cm^2 with 0.25 mAh/cm^2 loading[11].
